LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__Description: Maps Noble Architecture SketchUp tag names (the SSOT) to the runtime model category a loaded GLB lands in, to the short label the Model Layers panel shows, and to the edge style that category's projected linework starts with. One row per thing a person would want to switch off, or draw differently, in a drawing.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__PortedFrom: TrueVision3D 51__System__LayoutEditor/Na__LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Config__.json, 12-Sep-2026. The edge style fields and TrueVision's split building rows (1.1.0) on 13-Sep-2026.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__WhyThisDiffers: THE ONE FILE OF THE FEATURE THAT IS NOT SHARED, and the reason is the exports rather than the loader. ValeVision names each category after the GLB it came from: ValeVision__ plus the category the exporter wrote into the file name. A project exported with the building split by tag (Doous, 3047) therefore loads ValeVision__MainBuildingModel__ProposedWalls, ...ProposedRoofs, ...ProposedWindows and the rest - TrueVision's keys under the ValeVision__ prefix - and those rows are TrueVision's here, styles included. An older export arrives coarse, the whole existing building as ValeVision__MainBuildingModel__Existing and the whole proposal as ValeVision__MainBuildingModel__Proposed plus its doors, so the coarse rows stay as well. A row whose category a project did not load never appears. The panel, the module and the record shape are identical in both apps.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__EdgeStylesHere: Every row TrueVision has carries TrueVision's edge style value for value. The coarse Existing and Proposed rows take the style of structure - black, full weight - so in an older export the proposal's windows, and the existing building's openings, fixtures and furniture, draw at that weight until the project is exported again with the split. In a split export those same two keys hold only what is tagged 10__ExistingBuilding or 20__ProposedBuilding itself, which is structure, so the style still fits. Found 13-Sep-2026: this file first listed only the coarse rows, and Doous's windows drew black at full weight.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__HowThisIsUsed: The panel lists the categories the model ACTUALLY loaded, not this file: a category here with no GLB behind it never appears, and a category the model has that this file has not heard of still appears under an auto-generated label. This file supplies the wording, the grouping and the edge defaults, never the inventory.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__WhyKeyAndTag: Layer__CategoryKey is the runtime name - the THREE.Group the multi-model loader creates, and what the render, the linework exclusion and the per-segment owner tag all actually match on. Layer__SketchUpTags are the SSOT tag names an object carries in SketchUp, kept here so the two vocabularies stay traceable to each other when either side is renamed.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__WhyNoDefaultOff: Every category starts on. A viewport stores only what has been switched OFF, so a model that gains a category later shows it rather than silently hiding it.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__EdgeFields: Layer__EdgeWeightFactor, Layer__EdgeColour and Layer__EdgeLineType are the 2D PROJECTED LINEWORK style this category starts with in every newly drawn viewport. They apply to that layer and nothing else - not the 3D view, not the backing raster, not the markup. The colour and line type aliases are defined in Na__LayoutEditor__EdgeStyles__Config__.json.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__WeightMeaning: The weight is a FACTOR on the sheet's master viewport lineweight, never a width: 1.0 is the master exactly, 0.5 is half of it. Raising the master therefore thickens the whole drawing and leaves the hierarchy - walls over openings over fixtures over furniture - intact.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__DepthCueIntent: The greys are a depth cue, not decoration. Structure is black and full weight because it is what the drawing is about; openings and fixtures step back to dark grey; furniture and planting sit at mid and light grey because they are there for scale and should not compete with the thing being built.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__ExistingIsEqual: The Existing group deliberately carries the same weights and colours as Proposed (agreed 12-Sep-2026). Showing retained work lighter is a common convention but it is a drawing decision, not a data one; make it here, per row, when a job wants it.
LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Meta.Meta__PerViewport: These are DEFAULTS. A viewport that has had a category restyled stores only that category, in full, in Viewport__ProjectedEdges - so a change to this file moves every viewport that never disagreed.

LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__EdgeDefaults.EdgeDefaults__Description: What a row below inherits when it names no edge style of its own, and what a category the model loaded that this file has never heard of reads as. Black, solid, full weight: visible and obviously unstyled, rather than invisible.

Group__Layers.Layer__Note: In an older, coarse export this is the whole proposal except its doors (tags 20-24). In an export split by tag it holds only what is tagged 20__ProposedBuilding itself; the walls, floors, roofs and windows then load as the rows below.
In an older, coarse export this is the whole existing building (tags 10-19). In an export split by tag it holds only what is tagged 10__ExistingBuilding itself; the rest then loads as the rows below.

The whole model as one object, from a project exported before the tag ranges split it up. It is listed so those projects still get a switch; there is nothing finer to offer them, so it draws as structure does.

LayoutEditor__ModelLayers__Fallback.Fallback__Description: What a category the model loaded but this file does not list is called, and where it is put.
